resumen: With a single hip snap you take the kettlebell from between your legs all the way overhead, arm straight. One of the most technical ballistic kettlebell exercises.
ejecucion: Learn the one-arm swing and the clean first: the snatch combines them.
With your feet slightly wider than your hips and the kettlebell a hand’s length in front, grip the handle with one hand, push your hips back and hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward hard and guide the kettlebell up close to the body; as it passes chest height, punch your hand through the handle to catch it overhead without it hitting your forearm.
At the top, your arm is straight by your ear, with the bell resting on the back of your forearm and your body straight.
To lower, let the kettlebell drop in front, close to your body, and push your hips back only when your arm reaches your body; when you finish, switch hands.
If the kettlebell hits your forearm or your arm does not end up straight overhead, practise the clean and the press first.
If you lose control overhead, don’t try to save it: let go and step away. Keep the area around you clear.
When you finish, let it lose momentum and set it down with a straight back.
matices: In a study of twelve trained men doing snatches with a 24 kg kettlebell for six minutes, at peak acceleration the force on the kettlebell was about 800-900 N, and the ground force reached about 1,750 N, spread differently between the legs through the repetition; peak applied force dropped over the six minutes. In another, the snatch activated the opposite external oblique more and the erectors less than the one-arm swing.
